abstract: Microsoft reported strong FY24 Q3 financial results with total revenue of $61.9 billion (up 17%) and net income of $21.9 billion (up 20%), driven primarily by Microsoft Cloud revenue growth of 23% to $35.1 billion. The company's AI initiatives, particularly the Copilot stack and Azure OpenAI Service adoption across more than 65% of the Fortune 500, are fueling business expansion across productivity, cloud infrastructure, and personal computing segments.
keyFindings: Microsoft Cloud revenue reached $35.1 billion, up 23% year-over-year, with Azure and other cloud services revenue growing 31%.
Operating income increased 23% to $27.6 billion, while net income grew 20% to $21.9 billion in the quarter ended March 31, 2024.
More than 65% of the Fortune 500 now use Azure OpenAI Service, and $100M+ Azure deals increased over 80% year-over-year.
Azure-dependent segments showed strong growth: Intelligent Cloud revenue was $26.7 billion (up 21%), with server products and cloud services increasing 24%.
Microsoft returned $8.4 billion to shareholders through share repurchases and dividends in Q3 FY2024.
methodology: Financial results from Microsoft's official quarterly earnings release covering the period ended March 31, 2024, compared year-over-year to the corresponding quarter ended March 31, 2023. Data includes GAAP-reported figures with constant currency reconciliations provided separately. Results are presented across three business segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing.
qualifiers: Forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties including intense competition, execution risks in cloud services, cybersecurity threats, AI-related reputational risks, geopolitical conditions, and regulatory uncertainties.
